title: CargoWaves: The AI-Driven Inland Transport Platform Designed to Transform Logistics and Transport Industry
summary: DP World reports 30% higher cargo throughput and 20% lower CO2 per shipment through CargoWaves. AI’s contribution to the wider workflow improvement is unknown.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: DP World reports 30% higher cargo throughput and 20% lower CO2 per shipment through CargoWaves. The account provides no independent audit and does not separate AI’s contribution from booking, paperless processing, and workflow integration.
purpose: Match haulers, coordinate bookings, and improve inland cargo movement.
location: Platform deployment; individual operating ports unspecified

ratings.reason: DP World reports 30% greater cargo throughput and shorter processing and idle times. AI’s share of the broader workflow improvement is unknown.
The source claims 20% lower CO2 per shipment. This is a reported environmental improvement, with no measurement method or independent verification supplied.

ai_role.statement: AI recommends haulers and scheduling options. Digital booking, load coordination, paperless processing, and integration also contribute to the reported platform improvements.

evidence.citation: Project account in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. Outcomes are reported by the project team. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.

produced_by: Conditions that could produce the benefit are unspecified.
